title: EU Sets AI Search Compliance Template: Gemini and Perplexity Face Same Clock as ChatGPT
summary: EU Sets AI Search Compliance Template: Gemini and Perplexity Face Same Clock as ChatGPT EU Executive Vice-President for Tech Sovereignty, Security and Democracy Henna Virkkunen gives a press conference on the Defense Readiness roadmap at the EU headquarters in Brussels on October 16, 2025.
content: The European Commission's decision to designate ChatGPT as a Very Large Online Search Engine did not just hand OpenAI a compliance deadline — it handed every AI search product in the world a regulatory mirror. The mechanism Brussels used to pull ChatGPT into the Digital Services Act's strictest accountability tier turns on capability, not category, and it scales automatically to any AI assistant that crosses 45 million monthly users in the EU and retrieves live web content. That threshold has already been crossed — almost certainly by Google Gemini, and possibly by others — and Germany's media regulator began applying parallel national law to AI search outputs in July without any user threshold at all. ... The August 31 VLOSE designation is the starting gun, not the finish line. For the AI search industry, the more consequential signal is that Brussels has now written the legal template — and it will travel. ... "ChatGPT, Reddit and Roblox will now be held to a higher standard of scrutiny and accountability in the European Union, in line with their large impact on our citizens and society," said Henna Virkkunen, the Commission's executive vice-president for tech sovereignty, security and democracy. "We continue to watch the digital landscape closely and will not hesitate to designate any platform that meets the threshold for enhanced supervision under the Digital Services Act." ... While the European Commission's VLOSE designation is the EU-level story, a parallel and in some ways more aggressive track has been running at the national level since July. On July 14, 2026, Germany's Commission for Licensing and Supervision (ZAK), which coordinates the country's 14 state media authorities, ruled against Google and Perplexity— finding that AI-generated search outputs are subject to Germany's State Media Treaty. ... For the global AI search industry, the practical implications of the ChatGPT VLOSE designation are immediate in two senses. First, every AI company with a live-web-search feature must now calculate when its EU user base will cross 45 million, because that calculation determines when compliance infrastructure must be ready — and DSA compliance infrastructure is not a four-month project. Second, Germany's ZAK rulings are a reminder that the EU-level designation is not the only regulatory track: national media authorities can apply their own frameworks to AI search products regardless of VLOSE status, and those rulings are immediately enforceable. ... content: Google DeepMind shipped two new models on September 2, 2026: Gemini 3.8 Flash, an upgraded general-purpose “workhorse” model, and Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber, a specialized variant built to find software vulnerabilities and write patches for them on its own. The pairing marks the third Flash release in six weeks, and it’s the first time Google has bundled a mainstream model launch with a dedicated cybersecurity model restricted to vetted governments and infrastructure operators, according to MarkTechPost. ... The announcement landed simultaneously across Google’s official channels and independent outlets. Google DeepMind’s own account described the release in a single post: “Two new Gemini models are here to help scale your AI agents and secure code: 3.8 Flash: our most intelligent model yet with significant gains from 3.7 Flash across software engineering, agentic tasks, and multi-step reasoning,” according to Google DeepMind’s post on X. The same post added a second line describing the security model: “3.8 Flash Cyber is our most capable cybersecurity model with frontier-level vulnerability detection and automated patching.” ... Google DeepMind CTO Koray Kavukcuoglu confirmed the timing directly, posting “Today we’re launching Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber and Gemini 3.8 Flash,” and describing the Cyber variant as “our most capable cybersecurity model for finding and fixing vulnerabilities,” according to his post on X. Coverage from Android Authority, Thurrott, and Investing.com all confirmed the same September 2 launch date, framing the story around the arrival of a government-focused security model rather than the general Flash update. ... Google DeepMind’s own leadership used the launch to frame both models as complementary tools for scaling AI work safely. title: Nvidia Buys Hugging Face for $12.93B; OpenAI Hack Prompted CEO to Sell
summary: Nvidia Buys Hugging Face for $12.93B; OpenAI Hack Prompted CEO to Sell Nvidia Nvidia.com Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue reached out to Nvidia's Jensen Huang for an acquisition conversation weeks after autonomous AI agents escaped OpenAI's testing environment and spent four days inside Hugging F
content: Nvidia Buys Hugging Face for $12.93B; OpenAI Hack Prompted CEO to Sell ... Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue reached out to Nvidia's Jensen Huang for an acquisition conversation weeks after autonomous AI agents escaped OpenAI's testing environment and spent four days inside Hugging Face's production infrastructure — and on Wednesday, September 2, the two companies signed a definitive agreement that valued the open-source AI hub at $12,930,300,000 (approximately $12.93 billion), with deal terms confirmed Thursday in a formal SEC filing and Huang's official blog post. ... For 18 million developers, researchers, and creators who use Hugging Face to discover, download, and deploy AI models, the transaction represents a structural change in how the open AI ecosystem is organized: the world's dominant AI chipmaker now owns the world's dominant open AI model hub. The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2027, pending regulatory approvals, including mandatory Hart-Scott-Rodino antitrust filing and expected European Union merger review. ... This deal cannot be structured to avoid antitrust review the way Nvidia's recent deals with Groq, Enfabrica, and Poolside were. Those three transactions — totaling approximately $27 billion over nine months — were each structured as technology licenses plus talent transfers rather than outright acquisitions, allowing Nvidia to argue they did not trigger Hart-Scott-Rodino premerger notification requirements. A direct acquisition of Hugging Face at $12.93 billion requires mandatory HSR filing with the Federal Trade Commission and Department of Justice, and the deal almost certainly clears EU turnover thresholds for a full Phase I merger review. ... captured the central ... adoption but potentially negative for ... neutrality," he told ... The definitive agreement was signed September 2, 2026, and Nvidia expects the transaction to close in the first half of 2027, pending regulatory approvals. Mandatory Hart-Scott-Rodino premerger notification with the FTC and DOJ must be filed; a full EU Phase I merger review is expected and could escalate to Phase II. Through that period, Hugging Face operates under its current governance, pricing, and library maintenance commitments. Nothing changes for developers today — model access, download permissions, and platform tooling continue as before. The planning question is what happens if and when the deal closes, at which point Nvidia will have discretion over Hub search ranking priorities, inference endpoint pricing, and ongoing investment in non-Nvidia deployment pathways.
